summary: Croatia's Interior Ministry publishes victims and perpetrators of every Criminal Code article, including child sexual abuse, child pornography and violation of a child's rights, with a count of foreign citizens, and the statistics bureau publishes convictions by citizenship. That is a citizenship proxy on both sides; no ethnicity or national minority is recorded in crime data.

nations.National (Interior Ministry, DZS): Annual police statistical review; court-based conviction tables.

european_title: Not recorded by any Croatian crime source
european_note: Croatian crime statistics separate only foreign citizens from Croatian citizens. National minorities (Serbs, Roma and others) are counted in the census but not in any crime, victim or child-protection statistic, so neither ethnic Europeans nor any ethnic group can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Croatia records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity or national minority. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

breakdown.why: The Interior Ministry's 2025 statistical review gives, for sexual abuse of a child under 15 (Art. 158), 313 victims of whom 8 were foreign citizens and 129 perpetrators of whom 11 were foreigners. DZS convictions by citizenship: 121 adults convicted of child sexual abuse and exploitation, 9 with other citizenship. Croatian/foreign citizenship only.

Violation of a child's rights (Art. 177, abuse and neglect by carers): 3,190 victims (2,132 under 14), 70 foreign; 848 perpetrators, 37 foreigners. Domestic violence (Art. 179a): 2,600 victims (55 children), 88 foreign. Foreign victims are not split by age.

Art. 177 (violation of a child's rights, which covers neglect) and Art. 176 (abandoning a child: 8 victims, 1 foreign) give victims and perpetrators with a foreign-citizen count. Child-welfare statistics publish no citizenship.
Murder and aggravated murder: 103 victims (13 foreign; 5 under 14) and 97 perpetrators (13 foreigners) in 2025. Child victims are not split by citizenship.
Trafficking in human beings (Art. 106): 21 victims (3 aged 14-17; 12 foreign citizens of all ages) and 22 perpetrators (8 foreigners) in 2025.
Exploiting children for pornography (Art. 163): 275 child victims, 12 foreign; 176 perpetrators, 24 foreigners. Grooming (Art. 161): 16 victims.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Croatia scores 16% on the stricter scale (0-20%). The Interior Ministry publishes victims and perpetrators of each offence, including child sexual abuse and child pornography, with a count of foreign citizens, and DZS publishes convictions by citizenship. That is a citizenship proxy only; no ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
